estimation_procedure.description: Estimate a separate firm-level time-series regression for each firm. Each firm requires at least eight annual observations. The standard deviation of the residuals from each fitted regression is the firm-level accrual-quality measure. Table 3 Panel A summarizes coefficient distributions across 1,725 firms; its t-statistics are based on those cross-firm coefficient distributions.

In addition, we require at least eight years of data to estimate firm-specific regressions.

review_notes: The retained family is the firm-specific working-capital measurement regression in Equation (5), Table 3 Panel A. The paper says its theory is most naturally applied at firm level, the firm-specific specification is superior because coefficients likely differ across firms, and it proceeds with the firm-level model based on stronger theoretical grounding and empirical fit. Industry-specific and pooled panels are comparison designs; later tests use the residual-based construct and are applications.

The supplied reading includes independent, coordinator-verified transcriptions of Equation (5) and the working-capital construction. The displayed equation does not print deflators, while page 8 states that all variables are scaled by average total assets; the variable definitions preserve that global scaling. The item-code construction is retained in the verified signed-statement convention.

The underlying estimator is not named. Table 3 Panel A t-statistics summarize the cross-firm distribution of the 1,725 estimated coefficients; the paper does not identify an individual-fit standard-error correction or exact per-firm observation counts.
